summary: A card for a folding paper crown, and the page it opens. Twenty-four triangles in one strip, twisted into a short tower. It folds flat and springs open. Nobody has built one yet.
license_note: MIT is the parent repo's grant — LICENSE at the root of mrdirno/vibe-cards, spdx_id MIT from the anonymous GitHub licence API on 2026-08-17 (x-ratelimit-limit 60 proves the read was unauthenticated) — and it is the same licence this card's page declares in its #vc-card block. NOTICE, served at https://mrdirno.github.io/vibe-cards/NOTICE.txt, withholds several other cards' artwork from that grant; it does not withhold this one. Measured 2026-08-17: 'aurelia' occurs exactly once in NOTICE, at line 209, inside a quoted grep command in the Compound Craft section — never as a withheld path. Nothing in this manifest enlarges what NOTICE withholds, and nothing here withholds anything new. The card's #vc-card block declares replication 'open', so this card may be reproduced, including sold; that is the card's own term and this file repeats it rather than deciding it. What the grant RESTS ON is thinner than the grant, and is stated instead of hidden: the artwork arrived in a third-party drop that declares MIT only in its README's closing line, shipped no LICENSE file (`ls examples/*/LICENSE` returns aurea, bloom, manis and moku — not aurelia-card, measured 2026-08-17), and no file in this repo names who authored it. See origin.
origin: Not a fork and not a repository of its own: /aurelia/ is a page-project inside mrdirno/vibe-cards, published on that repo's Pages surface, and its MIT is INHERITED from the repo's LICENSE rather than chosen for this card. THE DESIGN DID NOT ORIGINATE HERE. examples/aurelia-card/ arrived as a finished outside drop that calls itself KIKKO CRAFTWORKS, run PB-49-14-07, and numbers itself 'CARD 04 — AURELIA KRESLING CORONA 01' (docs/README.md line 2, docs/AUTONOMOUS_HIERARCHY_LOG.md line 1); the README closes 'KIKKO CRAFTWORKS • OPEN SOURCE • MIT • 2026' (line 55). Both card images came out of an image model by the drop's own account — AUTONOMOUS_HIERARCHY_LOG.md line 18 lists 'Tools mobilized: image_gen editorial + blueprint' — and the front one shows a face, which the page and the #vc-card provenance field both declare is nobody real. The faces that actually print were composed IN this repo, not shipped by the drop: examples/aurelia-card/tools/build_card.py records that the drop's own vibe_card_front.png / vibe_card_back.png are 1034x660 against the 2022x1275 a 600 dpi trim needs, so the faces are rebuilt from its front_editorial.png and back_blueprint.png (1920x1280) instead. Three things were changed before anything was printed, all in commit 32184bf (2026-08-16, 'Two cards printable with nowhere to land'): the card was renumbered 001 → 005; its QR and chip payload were re-pointed off kikko.craftworks — that commit says it 'has no DNS record of any kind' — onto this url; and the code was regenerated and then decoded back out of the finished 600 dpi artwork, which src/site/network.json records under cards.destinations, card 'aurelia-card', surface 'qr' (`./tools/qrdecode` on all four shipped copies returns https://mrdirno.github.io/vibe-cards/aurelia/). The PAGE is inherited too, and says so in its own head comment: 'built on card 003's (src/site/moku/index.html) and card 004's (src/site/bloom/index.html) — same order, same register, same wishing well' (src/site/aurelia/index.html lines 36-38). So is the hardware it describes: the 12.0 mm tab into a 12.4 mm slot is cards 001 and 002's lock and the two-kiss-cut living hinge is card 004's, per the page's own 'What you already have' section. The wishing well is the repo's, shared with the other card pages, and is worked by tools/wishing_well.py.
_note: A page-project's manifest, so it lives at the surface's own url — the gate fetches <listed url>/wish-it-better.json — and `project` is the card id, the same string the chip carries in plaintext next to the address. L0, and each of its three clauses was measured at the live artifact on 2026-08-17 with a 404 control beside every 200: WISH_IT_BETTER.md is served at https://mrdirno.github.io/vibe-cards/WISH_IT_BETTER.md (200); the wish channel is this card's own page (200), carrying the data-wish-well marker §4 requires — one occurrence in the fetched bytes — account-free, and it QUEUES rather than mailing anyone (the well POSTs card_id 'AURELIA-CORONA-005' to a Supabase table, index.html line 849); LICENSE at the repo root returns spdx_id MIT anonymously. Controls: /aurelia/zz-control-2026-08-17-nonsense and /aurelia/control-404-for-the-wish-well-gate — the exact path verify_pages_artifact.mjs builds — both 404. NOT L1, and both failing clauses are measurements rather than judgement calls: (a) 'every shipped change carries an eval meeting §2' — `grep -ic aurelia docs/EVALS.md` returns 0, so nothing about this card is in the eval file; (b) 'wishes reach a terminal state' — the machinery exists repo-wide (tools/wishing_well.py moves new → building → shipped/declined and deletes nothing), but no wish for this card is recorded in any file readable here, and the private queue was NOT queried, so there is no evidence any wish for this card has reached any state. NOT L2 twice over: L2 requires L1 first, and §5 says the only amendment in force, v1.0.1, was found by the origin project and 'earns nobody L2'. WHY THIS FILE IS COMMITTED BEFORE THE LISTING: measured 2026-08-17, https://mrdirno.github.io/vibe-cards/aurelia/wish-it-better.json returned 404, 9379 bytes — byte-identical in size to two freshly-invented nonsense controls on the same host in the same run. Criterion 4 was UNMET at the url this card's chip carries. tools/build_site.py can DERIVE a manifest for an in-site project, but only for entries already in network.json listed[] (`in_site = [e for e in listed ...]`), so a derived manifest would be produced BY the act of listing and criterion 4 would be satisfied by listing itself; GT-001 avoided that by hand-authoring and committing first, which is the shape reproduced here. The builder keeps an authored manifest rather than overwriting it ('A HAND-AUTHORED MANIFEST OUTRANKS A DERIVED ONE'), and the rglob over src/site/ is what publishes this file. IF THIS CARD IS EVER LISTED, the level here and the level badged in src/site/network.json must be the same string: build_site.py fails the build on drift and verify_pages_artifact.mjs fails again in its network mode — moving one without the other breaks the deploy. THINGS AT THIS URL THAT DISAGREE WITH EACH OTHER, measured on this read-only pass and left unfixed: (1) the live #vc-card provenance field says 'Its panel labels are wrong; the panel count and the geometry are right', while the page body two sections down declines to say the count is right at all, and the page's own source comment explains why — 'a scan across the strip finds neither 22 nor 24 shapes and no measurement of the reduced picture can settle what the full sheet holds' (index.html lines 60-63; honesty section lines 719-729). Both ship from the same 200. The superseded arithmetic ('twenty-four labels, which is right') also survives in src/site/aurelia/entries.json line 13 and in examples/aurelia-card/tools/build_card.py's header — both added by commit 32184bf, whose own message re-measured the strip as TWENTY-TWO labels; entries.json is deleted from the built artifact (build_site.py line 453) and build_card.py is repo-only, so #vc-card is the only one of the three that is live. (2) The page's <h1> reads 'Aurelia Kresling Corona 01' in the fetched live bytes while its <title>, its #vc-card id and title, its footer and its own log entry all read 05 — and that log entry says the renumber was done 'before anything was printed and before the chip was written'. The supplied DRAWING legitimately keeps 01 in its title block per commit 32184bf; the page headline is the one that disagrees with its own page. NOT VERIFIED, named because this file's other fields would otherwise be read as covering it: (i) that the front render depicts nobody real — that is the page's declaration plus the drop's own 'image_gen' record, and no image was checked against any person; (ii) that the wishing well's public Supabase key can only INSERT — the page comment says 'That was tested, not assumed', and it was not re-tested here because testing it writes a row into a live production queue; (iii) who holds copyright in the supplied artwork — the drop declares MIT in one README line, ships no LICENSE, and names no author, while NOTICE withholds three OTHER cards that 'arrived from another system' with unrecorded authorship, so this card is treated differently from its nearest precedent and that difference rests on the drop's declaration alone; (iv) that a physical chip reads back this url — network.json's chip row for AURELIA-CORONA-005 is LEDGER-DERIVED from tools/card_ledger.py, not read back from a tag; (v) anything about the built object — nobody has printed, cut, folded or worn one, which the page says in its own first line, so every dimension, force and angle on it came off a drawing.
